title: Cannot map Co-pilot key to Ctrl (Right) properly
author: gluttony38

judgment.rationale: The report provides a concrete Copilot-key shortcut workaround and a VirtualBox failure with visible extra modifier transitions. An earlier maintainer answer confirms this hardware key must be mapped as a shortcut, so the remaining question is whether shortcut injection produces unmatched events in local key-state consumers or only in virtualized clients.
evidence: The reporter says direct key mapping warns and is ineffective, while a shortcut mapping works for Ctrl+C/X/V in some local applications.
VirtualBox does not recognize the mapped Right Ctrl host key and the reporter observed brief Right Ctrl, Left Win, and sometimes Shift transitions.
A second commenter reports a keyboard tester sees more than just Right Ctrl.
Maintainer guidance in #38358 says Copilot-key-to-Ctrl must be configured as a shortcut.
Keyboard Manager has recent fixes for stuck modifiers and remap lifecycle handling in KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the documented shortcut mapping in a key-event tester, a standard local control, and VirtualBox with a physical Right Ctrl control before selecting a targeted injection-lifecycle fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The shortcut configuration is established, but the evidence does not yet identify whether the observed extra modifiers originate in Keyboard Manager or in the Copilot-key/virtualization input stack.

issue_context.summary: A Copilot-key shortcut mapped to Right Ctrl works in some local controls but appears to produce extra modifier behavior and fails as a VirtualBox host key.
known_information: The report is on PowerToys 0.97.1 and Windows 11 Enterprise 26100.
A direct map showed a save warning; the shortcut configuration was based on #38358.
The author provided a video of the VirtualBox behavior.
Another commenter observed a keyboard tester reports a combination rather than only Right Ctrl.
inferences: The hardware Copilot sequence or shortcut remapping lifecycle may expose extra constituent modifiers to consumers, particularly virtualization software.
VirtualBox host-key handling may have requirements distinct from ordinary Ctrl shortcuts.
issue_context.analysis: The exact mapping and controls make this suitable for maintainer reproduction. Testing local event state before VirtualBox prevents incorrectly treating a hypervisor-specific limitation as a generic remapper defect.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and both comments.
Read #38358 and confirmed the maintainer's shortcut configuration guidance.
Inspected Keyboard Manager remap dispatch and recent history, including the stuck-modifier remap fix.
Searched live Copilot-key/VirtualBox reports; no direct active duplicate was found.

prerequisites: Use a device whose Copilot key emits the reported shortcut.
Configure the shortcut mapping to Right Ctrl as documented in #38358.
steps: Record physical Right Ctrl press/release in a key-event tester.
Record the mapped Copilot key press/release in the same tester.
Compare Ctrl+C/X/V in a standard desktop application.
Configure VirtualBox to use Right Ctrl as host key and compare physical versus mapped key behavior.
Trace injected and physical event order if extra Win, Shift, or unmatched state appears.
reproduce.expected_result: The mapped key exposes one matched Right Ctrl down/up pair and behaves equivalently to physical Right Ctrl where the host accepts it.
setup_requirements: Use a non-sensitive test VM and record the exact Keyboard Manager shortcut mapping.
